subject: Dedicated capacity intake: session matrix + demo profile
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Lucy Huang <lucy@latticeai.com>, Tom Rivera <tom.rivera@latticeai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 May 2025 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated capacity intake: session matrix + demo profile

Hi Lucy / Tom —

Thanks for the time last week. Ahead of the dedicated-capacity demo and sizing walkthrough, could you take a pass on the attached session matrix template and the prompt/profile examples? The goal is to capture the live traffic shape so we can:

- estimate steady vs burst committed capacity,
- recommend GPU SKU + quantization tradeoffs, and
- propose a safe autoscale & burst policy for your SLA.

What would be most helpful from you:
1) A filled session matrix (attached CSV) with expected requests per minute by hour (or sample day),
2) Distribution of prompt length (tokens) and response length (tokens) — mean / p50 / p95,
3) Percent of requests that reuse KV cache/multi-turn sessions vs stateless single-shot, and typical session duration,
4) Your target latency SLOs (p50/p95) and any hard upper bound on acceptable tail latency,
5) Any upcoming events (marketing launch, batch jobs) that create predictable bursts (dates and expected burst magnitude).

If easier, you can drop a sample export from a day (CSV is fine) and we’ll translate it into the template. I’ve attached a short PDF with example prompt profiles to show how we bucket call types for sizing.

Can you aim to return the template by EOD Thursday so we can run a quick capacity BOE and bring numbers into tomorrow’s demo?

Attachments: session_matrix_template.csv, prompt_profile_examples.pdf

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123

Marissa — thanks, this is great. Appended below are high-level answers and I attached a small sample export (sample_traffic_export.csv) from last Thursday for context. I’ll ask our infra team for the full hourly breakdown but wanted to get these numbers to you ASAP.

Quick profile (high-level):
- Typical steady traffic: ~350 requests/min (global, aggregated)
- Peak burst: ~5,000 requests/min for short windows (5–15 minutes) during product announce spikes; predictable and tied to marketing events
- Prompt lengths: mean 120 tokens, p50 95 tokens, p95 420 tokens
- Response lengths: mean 300 tokens, p50 210 tokens, p95 1200 tokens (long generation when users request detailed code explanations)
- Multi-turn sessions: ~30% of calls; average session length 45s, median 30s — we do KV caching for user sessions
- Mix: 60% single-shot QA/lookup, 25% multi-turn assistant, 15% batch/long-run generation (async flows)
- Target latency: p50 <= 120ms, p95 <= 400ms for interactive flows; for async batch flows the tolerance is higher (seconds)

We can deliver the CSV with hourly counts by EOD Thursday. Also attaching a small sample (sample_traffic_export.csv) here for you to use.

Let me know if you need additional signal (eg logs with token counts).

Best,
Lucy Huang
Head of Platform, LatticeAI
lucy@latticeai.com

Sending Lucy’s reply and sample export — seems we have enough to run a first pass BOE for SKU recommendation and suggested commit size. Key asks for the sizing run:

- Confirm GPU SKU choice for sustained 350rpm with 5krpm 10–15m bursts (recommend one conservative and one cost-optimized path),
- Consider multi-turn cache reuse — that should reduce per-token cost for the 30% sessions; model selection/kv cache policy will matter,
- Suggest quantization level we can support for their p95 latency target without sacrificing quality for long generations,
- Draft a short mutually actionable timeline for pilot -> commit (eg pilot 4 weeks, canary traffic window, then reserved commit),
- Populate the HubSpot deal (HSP-1839) with the BOE summary and next steps — I’ll include the template in the call.

Lucy’s top-level numbers (from her email):
> Typical steady traffic: ~350 requests/min
> Peak burst: ~5,000 requests/min for 5–15 minutes
> Prompt mean 120 tokens / response mean 300 tokens
> 30% multi-turn sessions with avg 45s duration
> Target p95 <= 400ms for interactive flows

Ben / Karthik — can you each take one of the two SKU paths? Ben: conservative (higher headroom, NVL-8192-style), Karthik: cost-optimized (quantized 8-bit mixed precision candidate). Aim to return BOE numbers by EOD so I can fold into the demo tomorrow. I’ll shepherd the HubSpot notes and schedule a 30-min follow-up.

Thanks —
Marissa

Marissa — I’ll take the conservative SKU path. Quick back-of-envelope (assumptions inline):

Assumptions:
- Model baseline: 13B with standard FP16 kernels (no heavy quant), average generation cost proportional to tokens,
- Avg end-to-end tokens per request: 420 tokens (prompt+response) per Lucy’s numbers,
- Steady: 350 rpm -> ~5.8 requests/sec; Peak burst: 5,000 rpm -> ~83.3 requests/sec
- Multi-turn reuse reduces work for 30% of requests by ~35% on token decoding cost due to KV cache reuse

Conservative BOE:
- Recommend reserved pool: 6 GPUs (NVL-like A100 80GB equivalent) with autoscale + burst pool (additional 10 GPUs cold-start for marketing spikes) — gives comfortable headroom for p95 under 400ms for interactive flows,
- If we assume 6 GPUs serving steady and autoscale to +10 for bursts, estimate monthly committed tokens cost and unit economics in the BOE spreadsheet (attached: capacity_back_of_envelope.xlsx),
- For p95 target, keep FP16 kernels and avoid aggressive 4-bit quant for the pilot; we can evaluate 8-bit mixed precision in the cost-optimized path.

Action items:
1) Karthik: run the cost-optimized run and share a parallel spreadsheet,
2) Marissa: I’ll upload my BOE to the HubSpot deal and schedule a 30-min sync for tomorrow 10:00am PT — does that work for Lucy’s team?

I’ll share the spreadsheet now; if we need a faster answer I can swap to smaller batch sizing per GPU and provide per-GPU throughput curves.

Cheers,
